phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Level diagram for a resonantly driven two-level emitter with coherent coupling Omega and decay kappa; it is explanatory geometry rather than a plotted numerical observable.

For kappa=4 Omega, reproduce the plotted scaled cumulant-generating function theta(s), activity k(s)=-theta'(s), and constant Mandel parameter Q(s)=-2/3 over the shown s range; the paper gives theta(s)=-2 Omega[1-exp(-s/3)] and k(s)=2 Omega exp(-s/3)/3.

Reproduce the large-deviation rate curve -phi(k), phi(k)=3[k ln(k/k0)-(k-k0)], and its contrast with a Poisson curve; equivalently verify the claimed nu=3 Conway-Maxwell-Poisson photon-count law proportional to Poisson(K;t)^3.
phase1_inventory.source_ref: Fig. 1(C), caption, and text following Eq. (5)

phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Generate representative photon-jump point processes for the three biased subensembles marked k=2, k=2/3, and k=2/9, showing rate-rescaled trajectory statistics at the special kappa=4 Omega point.
Three-level level diagram with drives Omega1 and Omega2 and decay kappa1; it specifies the model topology but is not itself a numerical result.

For kappa1=4 Omega1 and Omega2=Omega1/10, directly diagonalize the tilted generator and reproduce theta(s), its agreement with the two-level branch for s<0, departure near s=0, and inactive-side asymptote theta(s much greater than 0) approximately -kappa1 Omega2^2.

Reproduce the crossover curves k(s) and Q(s)/10, including the active-side two-level behavior, Q approaching -2/3 for s much less than 0, inactive k approaching zero and Q approaching 0 for s much greater than 0, and the fluctuation peak near s=0.
Reproduce the photon-count large-deviation curve t^-1 ln Pt(k)=-phi(k) and Poisson comparator, including the asymmetric fat low-k tail and thin high-k tail attributed to inactive and active regimes.
Generate representative inactive and active photon-jump trajectories with the displayed mean rates k=0.02 and k=0.74 and verify intermittency/coexistence of bright and dark periods at s=0.
Schematic of pumped atoms traversing a thermally coupled cavity and changing the photon number from N to N+1; it describes the apparatus/model rather than numerical output.

For pump parameter alpha=1.2 pi, reproduce theta(s) and k(s)/10 and locate the first-order activity jump at a negative counting field, demonstrating dynamical coexistence away from normal s=0 dynamics.
For alpha=2 pi, reproduce theta(s) and k(s)/10 with a cusp and discontinuous activity jump at s=0, separating high-activity and low-activity phases at normal-dynamics coexistence.

Reproduce the three cavity photon-number distributions rho_s(N) intended to show active, coexistence/stationary, and inactive phases. The printed panel labels the top curve s=-0.05, the middle s=0, and the bottom s=-0.05 even though the caption requires opposite activity sides; the label/sign must therefore be tested rather than silently normalized.

Verify that the biased density operator obeys the tilted master equation W_s in Eq. (4), that theta(s) is its largest-real-part eigenvalue, and that derivatives -theta'(s) and -theta''(s)/theta'(s)-1 generate the stated activity and Mandel statistics.

Independently rederive the l_s similarity/Doob transform in Eqs. (6)-(7), check complete positivity and trace preservation of the transformed Lindblad dynamics, and verify that typical jumps under tilde L1 realize the original s-biased trajectory ensemble.

For the special two-level point kappa=4 Omega, verify that the transformed Hamiltonian and jump amplitude scale as exp(-s/3) and exp(-s/6), respectively, so all rates scale by exp(-s/3) and rare trajectories become typical after t maps to exp(s/3)t.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: An independently assembled 4x4 tilted superoperator reproduces Eq. (5), its activity derivative, and Q=-2/3 at the printed kappa/Omega ratio; the attested frozen CSV is consistent with that independent calculation.
target_reviews.formula_reason: Eqs. (1), (4), and (5) give the implemented matrix and closed form without an unstated physical input.
target_reviews.parameter_reason: Omega is a time unit and kappa=4 Omega is printed; the plotted s domain does not change the physical model.

independent_checks.claim: A matrix-basis action implementation, not the bundled Kronecker implementation, gives theta(s) equal to -2[1-exp(-s/3)] at s=-5,-1,0,1,5 with maximum absolute difference 1.8e-15.
At s=0 the independently constructed generator has theta=0 and the analytic derivatives give k=2/3 and Q=-2/3.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The agreement was produced by copying the printed closed form while the generic tilted Liouvillian used a wrong vectorization or eigenvalue branch.
falsification_attempts.method: Construct W_s by applying the master equation directly to every matrix unit E_ij, diagonalize it at five separated s values, and compare it with both Eq. (5) and the frozen theta_eigen column.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: The Legendre-Fenchel maximizer can be solved analytically and yields exactly the printed factor-three rate function; the configured grid contains every optimizer over the reproduced k range.
target_reviews.formula_reason: Substituting k=-theta'(s) into the dual gives phi(k)=3[k ln(k/k0)-(k-k0)] with k0=2 Omega/3.
target_reviews.parameter_reason: The figure is scale-free after Omega=1 and uses the printed k0 relation; the numerical k and s ranges cover the source panel and all stationary dual points.

independent_checks.claim: Solving d[-sk-theta(s)]/ds=0 gives s*=-3 ln(k/k0); substitution reproduces the printed phi and the frozen grid result differs by at most 2.42e-6.
The reproduced rate function is nonnegative and has its zero minimum at k0, as required for a normalized large-deviation law.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The apparent agreement is a boundary artifact of the finite s grid.
falsification_attempts.method: Evaluate s*=-3 ln(k/k0) at both reproduced k endpoints; every optimizer lies strictly within the configured [-8,14] interval, then compare the analytic and grid dual columns.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: All three event records have the requested activities within ordinary finite-record fluctuations and retain the non-Poissonian waiting-time statistics implied by Q=-2/3.
target_reviews.formula_reason: The exact two-level Doob/time-rescaling identity makes each requested biased activity a physical trajectory of the same dimensionless model.
target_reviews.parameter_reason: The three printed activities 2, 2/3, and 2/9 are used exactly; duration and seeds only select representative finite records because the source supplies no unique trajectory array.

independent_checks.claim: Counts 593, 195, and 66 over duration 300 give rates 1.9767, 0.6500, and 0.2200; using Fano factor 1/3, all count residuals are below 0.62 standard deviations.
The empirical squared coefficients of variation of waiting times are 0.324, 0.362, and 0.271, close to the scale-invariant 1/3 rather than the Poisson value 1.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The plotted records are rate-matched Poisson processes and therefore do not reproduce the paper's antibunched scale-invariant trajectories.
falsification_attempts.method: Recompute every inter-event interval from the frozen CSV and compare its coefficient of variation with the Poisson and Q=-2/3 predictions.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: An independent matrix-basis 9x9 diagonalization reproduces the active branch, crossover, and inactive perturbative plateau for the printed three-level model.
target_reviews.formula_reason: The Hamiltonian, counted jump, and dominant-eigenvalue prescription follow directly from the source and give a trace-preserving s=0 generator.
target_reviews.parameter_reason: kappa1=4 Omega1 and Omega2=Omega1/10 are printed; Omega1=1 only fixes units.

independent_checks.claim: Direct action on the nine matrix units reproduces sampled frozen theta values exactly to displayed precision and gives theta(0)=4.39e-16.
The independent generator approaches theta=-0.04127 at s=10 versus the paper's leading small-Omega2 estimate -kappa1 Omega2^2=-0.04, while the negative-s branch approaches the two-level result.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The inactive plateau has the wrong sign or scale because the weak drive or counted jump was attached to the wrong transition.
falsification_attempts.method: Assemble the three-state Hamiltonian and L1 from the source, evaluate the dominant eigenvalue out to s=10, and compare the limit with -kappa1 Omega2^2.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: The activity drop and positive Mandel peak persist under an independently chosen higher-order derivative stencil, so they are not artifacts of the bundled finite-difference step.
target_reviews.formula_reason: k=-theta' and Q=-theta''/theta'-1 are the correct cumulant identities for the paper's e^{-sK} convention.
target_reviews.parameter_reason: The physical ratios are printed and used exactly; derivative step is a converged numerical choice rather than a paper parameter.

independent_checks.claim: A five-point derivative with h=1e-4 gives Q=11.36169 at s=0.074, Q=-0.66235 at s=-0.5, and the same activity curve as the frozen h=5e-5 data.
Independent evaluation toward large negative s recovers Q approximately -2/3, while positive-s activity tends to zero and Q tends toward zero.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The large Q peak is numerical differentiation noise near a small first derivative.
falsification_attempts.method: Recompute theta from an independently assembled generator and differentiate with a five-point stencil and a doubled step; compare peak location and height with the frozen curve.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: Continuous one-dimensional optimization of the independently generated SCGF reproduces the frozen rate curve, its zero at the physical activity, and the lower cost of low-activity deviations.
target_reviews.formula_reason: The Legendre-Fenchel convention is consistent with Z_t(s)=sum_K P_t(K)e^{-sK} and with the source's sign convention.
target_reviews.parameter_reason: All physical three-level parameters are printed and exact; the dual grids are numerical convergence choices.

independent_checks.claim: Bounded continuous optimization over s agrees with the frozen grid dual to below 8e-4 at representative k values from 0.02 to 0.94 and places the minimum at k=0.3992.
At equal deviations 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3 from the physical activity, the low-k rate cost is smaller than the high-k cost, independently confirming the claimed fat low-k and thin high-k tails.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The claimed tail asymmetry is a plotting impression without a rate-function difference.
falsification_attempts.method: Compute the dual by continuous optimization and compare phi(k0-delta) with phi(k0+delta) for three deltas, holding the distance from the physical activity fixed.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: The two displayed activities occur as finite windows of physical s=0 blinking trajectories under an independent event-driven Monte Carlo-wave-function implementation and multiple fresh seeds.
target_reviews.formula_reason: The no-jump Hamiltonian and sole radiative jump follow from the printed three-level Lindblad model.
target_reviews.parameter_reason: The paper supplies both physical ratios and the representative rates; duration and seeds are reproducibility choices because no author event array is claimed.

independent_checks.claim: An event-driven waiting-time solver, rather than the bundled fixed-step solver, generated 4000-time-unit records for three new seeds; 100-unit windows reached rates near 0.02 and 0.74 in every run.
Across three independent seeds the long-record rates were 0.3805, 0.39325, and 0.41125 and the sliding-window ranges covered inactive and active regimes, excluding a single-seed coincidence.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: Exact k=0.02 and k=0.74 windows arise only from cherry-picking one anomalous discretized seed rather than physical intermittency.
falsification_attempts.method: Use exact non-Hermitian waiting-time sampling with three different seeds, then scan 100-unit windows at five-unit stride for both activities.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: The reconstructed negative-s transition is numerically stable for the chosen later-paper parameters, but the original Letter omits N_ex and thermal occupation and its printed L1 lowers photon number while the code silently uses an atomic-birth process.
target_reviews.formula_reason: Under the annihilation-operator convention used earlier in the same Letter, the printed f(aa-dagger)a sends |n> to |n-1>; the implemented atomic_birth sends n to n+1 and corresponds to the corrected a-dagger f(aa-dagger) operator printed in the later same-author paper.
target_reviews.parameter_reason: alpha=1.2 pi is printed, but N_ex=100 and nu=0.15 come only from arXiv:1103.0919 and are not identified there as the exact hidden parameters of this Letter's Fig. 3.

independent_checks.claim: A nonsymmetric sparse birth-death eigensolver agrees with the frozen theta values at s=-0.1,-0.05,0,0.05,0.1 to at most 1.6e-12 for the declared reconstruction.
Sweeping plausible omitted N_ex and nu values changes the off-zero transition location and stationary weights, so the declared reconstruction cannot establish a paper-exact Fig. 3(B).

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The implementation follows the micromaser jump operator printed in the target Letter.
falsification_attempts.method: Apply the printed L1 to number states using the Letter's earlier annihilation convention and compare the resulting n-to-n-1 support with the n-to-n+1 lower diagonal implemented as atomic_birth.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The negative-s transition is a numerical eigensolver artifact for the declared reconstructed parameters.
falsification_attempts.method: Build the nonsymmetric generator directly and solve it with a sparse general eigensolver at five anchors instead of the symmetrized tridiagonal route.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: The s=0 cusp survives independent numerical solution for the reconstructed model, but the same unproven parameter identity and printed-operator/code mismatch prevent a paper-exact adjudication.
target_reviews.formula_reason: EQ007 and EQ008 cannot both follow from the Letter's printed lowering-form L1; the code uses the physically corrected raising process without recording a verified source correction in the formula verdict.
target_reviews.parameter_reason: alpha=2 pi is exact, but the two scale-setting micromaser parameters are supplied by a later paper rather than identified for this panel in 0911.0556.

independent_checks.claim: A direct nonsymmetric sparse generator reproduces the five frozen anchor theta values for alpha=2 pi to about 1.2e-13 and locates the sharp activity change at s=0.
At s=0 the independently constructed birth-death generator conserves probability and has dominant eigenvalue zero for the reconstructed parameters.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The apparent s=0 transition is created by the symmetric tridiagonal similarity rather than the original nonsymmetric generator.
falsification_attempts.method: Solve the nonsymmetric sparse generator directly on both sides of zero and compare its dominant branch with the frozen curve.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The code implements the Letter's printed atomic jump without alteration.
falsification_attempts.method: Evaluate the printed operator on |n> and compare its number-state direction with the implemented birth term and the later same-author corrected operator.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: The reconstructed distributions are normalized and phase ordered, but their stationary peak ratio is highly sensitive to the two omitted parameters; moreover, the source panel prints the negative bias twice while the reproduction silently uses +0.05 for the inactive curve.
target_reviews.formula_reason: The frozen distributions are generated from an atomic-birth operator that is not the literal L1 transcribed as verified in EQ007.
target_reviews.parameter_reason: N_ex and nu are absent from 0911.0556; later-paper values give only a 0.0071 secondary-to-primary stationary peak ratio and do not uniquely identify the original panel.

independent_checks.claim: All three frozen distributions sum to one and have nonnegative entries; their means are 69.885, 18.693, and 17.815 for s=-0.05,0,+0.05.
The exact s=0 product recursion printed in the later paper reproduces the frozen stationary distribution with L1 distance 5.4e-11 for the declared reconstructed parameters.
Changing omitted N_ex and nu over plausible values changes the stationary peak ratio by orders of magnitude, so the panel's relative weights are not paper-exact evidence.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The upper and lower distinct Fig. 3(D) curves can both correspond to s=-0.05 under one fixed micromaser generator, as printed.
falsification_attempts.method: Compare the two source labels with the text's s<0 high-photon and s>0 low-photon phase ordering; then solve the same generator at -0.05 and +0.05 and compare the means with the frozen distributions.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The reconstructed stationary distribution quantitatively establishes the visibly bimodal paper panel.
falsification_attempts.method: Compute the secondary-to-primary peak ratio and repeat the exact stationary recursion while varying the omitted N_ex and nu; test whether the peak weights are stable.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: The generalized similarity transform is trace preserving by direct adjoint algebra and by an independent left-eigenmatrix calculation; the special two-level rate scaling also follows from Eq. (5) and matches the frozen data.
target_reviews.formula_reason: If W_s^dagger(l_s)=theta l_s, the transformed adjoint annihilates the identity; the biased jump prefactor and positive similarity yield the stated Lindblad/Doob process.
target_reviews.parameter_reason: The check uses the fully specified two-level special point and biases s=-1,0,1; no micromaser reconstruction enters this target.

independent_checks.claim: Applying the adjoint of S W_s S^-1-theta I to the identity reduces exactly to S^-dagger[W_s^dagger(l_s)-theta l_s]=0, proving trace preservation.
A direct adjoint eigenproblem at s=-1,0,1 yields positive l_s and trace residuals below 6.4e-15; the activities match (2/3)exp(-s/3) within 6.5e-11.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The similarity transform only shifts the dominant eigenvalue but fails to define a trace-preserving physical generator.
falsification_attempts.method: Solve the left adjoint eigenproblem independently, form the positive square-root similarity, subtract theta, and evaluate the identity left-zero-mode residual at three biases.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The claimed two-level time rescaling has the wrong sign in exp(-s/3).
falsification_attempts.method: Differentiate the independently verified Eq. (5), compare k(s)/k(0) at s=-1 and +1 with exp(-s/3), and compare to the frozen Doob summaries.

findings.claim: T008-T010 do not have a valid paper-to-code formula gate: the Letter and EQ007 print L1 proportional to f(aa-dagger)a, which lowers photon number in the convention used earlier in the same paper, while the implementation uses an n-to-n+1 atomic birth corresponding to the later corrected a-dagger f(aa-dagger) operator.
reproduction_steps: Read the micromaser L1 in paper/paper-source/qjumps-submit.tex and the annihilation convention in the two-level section.
Apply the printed operator to a number state |n>; its support is |n-1>, whereas Fig. 3(A) and the physical atom-decay description require |n+1>.
Inspect atomic_birth and the lower diagonal in implementation/src/quantum_jumps/micromaser.py; they implement n-to-n+1.
Compare with Eq. (3) of paper/raw/external_references/1103.0919.pdf, which places a-dagger on the raising jump.

findings.claim: T008-T010 are not paper-exact because 0911.0556 does not specify N_ex or the thermal occupation; N_ex=100 and nu=0.15 are imported from a later same-author paper that does not identify them as the hidden parameter pair for this Letter's Fig. 3.
reproduction_steps: Search paper/paper-source/qjumps-submit.tex for N_ex, excitation_number, thermal_occupation, and a numerical relation fixing r, kappa, and lambda; none fixes the two dimensionless values.

Inspect implementation/parameter_provenance.json and implementation/config/paper_reconstructed.json to confirm that the values are sourced from arXiv:1103.0919 and the run is classified mixed/reconstructed.

Rebuild the number-basis generator from the printed jump structure and vary N_ex and nu; observe changes in the alpha=1.2 pi transition position and orders-of-magnitude changes in stationary peak ratios.

findings.claim: Fig. 3(D) is internally inconsistent: two distinct distributions are both labelled s=-0.05, while the paper text assigns high-photon activity to s<0 and low-photon inactivity to s>0. The reproduction's use of +0.05 for the lower curve is scientifically plausible but cannot be silently treated as the literal paper claim or promoted to paper_error_candidate while F001 and F002 remain open.
reproduction_steps: Extract or visually inspect paper/paper-source/fig3.pdf and record the three printed labels from top to bottom.
Read the micromaser paragraph in paper/paper-source/qjumps-submit.tex that maps s<0 to large photon occupation and s>0 to small occupation.
Group generated_data/outputs/data/micromaser_distributions.csv by s and verify that the high-photon mean is at -0.05 and the low-photon mean is at +0.05.
Confirm in generated_data/outputs/data/quantitative_claims.json that the reproducer itself classifies this as an inconclusive source-label discrepancy.

findings.claim: The pixel-evidence artifact marks T008-T010 scientific regions lifecycle_eligible even though authored target claims declare their parameter match unknown; visual similarity under reconstructed parameters cannot satisfy a paper-exact lifecycle gate.
reproduction_steps: Read contracts/target_claims.json and record claimed_parameter_match=unknown for T008, T009, and T010.
Read the corresponding entries in machine_evidence/outputs/checks/pixel_evidence.json and record lifecycle_eligible=true.
Compare with implementation/config/paper_reconstructed.json, which classifies the micromaser settings as reconstructed and the overall parameter match as mixed.

findings.claim: The independently inventoried numeric item claim_ld_spectral_construction is absent as a canonical authored coverage item and has no dedicated authored target; existing formula dependencies do not provide the required inventory-to-target scope row.
reproduction_steps: Locate claim_ld_spectral_construction in protocol.phase1_inventory and figure_inventory.
Inspect contracts/numerical_scope_claims.json and confirm that no authored item names this quantitative claim.
Inspect contracts/target_claims.json and confirm that no target is scoped as the standalone LD spectral construction claim; do not create a reviewer-invented target.

findings.claim: The independently inventoried numeric item claim_two_level_mapped_time_rescaling is absent as a canonical authored coverage item and has no dedicated authored target; T011 contains a related check but the authored scope merges it into a broader mapping item instead of covering the frozen inventory row.
reproduction_steps: Locate claim_two_level_mapped_time_rescaling in protocol.phase1_inventory and figure_inventory.
Inspect contracts/numerical_scope_claims.json and confirm that only the broader Rare-to-typical mapping quantitative identities item is authored.
Inspect T011 in contracts/target_claims.json, preserve the new Phase-1 item as a blocking scope finding, and do not invent T012.
